prepared_by: Pre-event research draft (see research/flock-laws.md and research/flock-data.md). Agent B owns this file from kickoff: verify needs_check items, then improve.

hops.what_moves: Plate image, plate number, time, location, vehicle attributes

rules.summary: A vendor hosting the data is not counted as 'sharing' under state law, which is how Flock's cloud is legal.
rules.quote: the provision of data hosting or towing services shall not be considered the sale, sharing, or transferring of ALPR information.
rules.citation: Cal. Civil Code §1798.90.55(b) (SB 34), quoted in CA DOJ Bulletin 2023-DLE-06

rules.summary: SFPD's policy binds vendors working for the City, including Flock.
rules.quote: Employees, consultants, volunteers, and vendors while working on behalf of the City with the Department are required to comply with this Policy.
rules.citation: SFPD ALPR Surveillance Technology Policy, Purpose and Scope

rules.summary: Flock says the police agency, not Flock, owns the plate reads.
rules.quote: LPR data gathered by the Flock Safety system on behalf of Flock Safety customers is owned by the customer.
rules.citation: Flock LPR Usage & Privacy Policy (last updated June 30, 2026)

retention.summary: Flock held SF data for 12 months until Mayor Lurie's Sept 2026 rules required Flock to delete after 30 days. Flock's new default is 7 days, but it reportedly applies to new customers only.

breaches.summary: Flock units are classed as ALPRs rather than 'public safety cameras', so they skip that ordinance's hearing and reporting rules.

hops.notes: Contract: about $3.9M, Feb 20 2024 to Feb 19 2027 (SF Standard). Board votes on extension Feb 2027. Contract text itself not found.
hops.plain: Your plate is photographed and uploaded to Flock, a private company that hosts it for SFPD.

hops.what_moves: Search results and hotlist alerts for SFPD officers and analysts

rules.summary: SFPD may use ALPR data only for the use cases its Board-approved policy lists.
rules.quote: No SFPD member shall access ALPR data for any use other than the authorized use cases herein
rules.citation: SFPD ALPR policy (Ordinance 255-23, approved Dec 12, 2023), Policy Statement

rules.summary: An ALPR alert alone is not grounds for a stop; it must be verified first.
rules.quote: Officers shall not stop a vehicle solely based on an ALPR alert.

rules.summary: Every search must carry an incident number, dispatch number or stated reason (Department Notice 26-011).
rules.quote: must enter an incident number, dispatch call number or stated reason for every search

rules.summary: SF's surveillance ordinance requires a Board-approved policy before a department uses surveillance technology.
rules.quote: a Department must obtain Board of Supervisors approval by ordinance of a Surveillance Technology Policy

retention.summary: SFPD keeps ALPR data 12 months, or 5 years if tied to a criminal investigation. Since Sept 2026, access to data older than 30 days needs leadership approval.

breaches.summary: An officer searched Flock for a spouse's stolen car and posted Flock images on social media; referred to Internal Affairs as a conflict of interest.

hops.notes: SFPD says its 12-month retention 'defers to the NCRIC retention standard', but NCRIC's own 2024 policy says its vendor's 30-day cap prevails. Good contradiction to show.
hops.plain: SFPD officers search those reads. Each search must have a case number or a stated reason.

hops.what_moves: SFPD's ALPR data pooled in a regional repository that NCRIC-approved agencies can query

rules.summary: Sharing with another California public agency is allowed under state law.
rules.quote: A public agency shall not sell, share, or transfer ALPR information, except to another public agency, and only as otherwise permitted by law.
rules.citation: Cal. Civil Code §1798.90.55(b), quoted in CA DOJ Bulletin 2023-DLE-06

rules.summary: NCRIC may share only with California state or local law enforcement.
rules.quote: NCRIC may only share, disseminate, or provide access to ALPR information to California state or local law enforcement agencies.

rules.summary: The agency that collected the data stays its owner and custodian.
rules.quote: The originating agency retains control and ownership as the official custodian of its records.

retention.summary: NCRIC allows up to 365 days, but says the shortest applicable limit wins and its vendor caps retention at 30 days.

breaches.summary: SFPD's May 2026 audit found 299 queries (May 2025 to May 2026) run by WSIN analysts, using access NCRIC had shared, on behalf of federal and out-of-state agencies. Chief Lew cut off NCRIC's access.

hops.notes: NCRIC is no longer in SFPD's current outbound sharing list (DeFlock/EyesOnFlock snapshot, 2026-11-16), consistent with the cutoff.
hops.plain: SFPD shared access with a regional fusion center that is supposed to serve only California police.

hops.what_moves: Plate searches against SF's camera network

rules.summary: The Attorney General reads SB 34 as banning sharing with out-of-state, federal or private entities, including through vendor databases.
rules.quote: SB 34 does not permit California LEAs to share ALPR information with private entities or out-of-state or federal agencies, including out-of-state and federal law enforcement agencies.

rules.summary: SFPD bars out-of-state and federal transfers unless a California court orders it. The court-order exception is SFPD's wording, not the statute's.
rules.quote: ALPR information shall not be sold, shared, or transferred to out-of-state or federal agencies without a court order or warrant issued by a California court.

rules.summary: State and local staff may not help out-of-state investigations of legally protected abortion or gender-affirming care.
rules.quote: shall not cooperate with or provide information to any individual

retention.summary: Not applicable: out-of-state agencies should not receive the data at all.

breaches.summary: From about Aug 2024 to Feb 2025, Flock's Nationwide Lookup let out-of-state agencies query SF's network. SFPD says Flock enabled it without the Department's knowledge or authorization.

SF Standard's review of SFPD search logs (public records) counted more than 1.6 million searches of SF's plate data by nearly 4,000 out-of-state agencies, Aug 2024 to Feb 2025, at least 19 marked ICE-related.

Allegation: a class action filed by Gibbs Mura (Feb 2026) claims federal and out-of-state agencies obtained Flock plate data more than 1.6 million times over seven months. Flock says it will vigorously defend itself.

SF's Human Rights Commission found no sanctuary-law violation by SFPD, since Flock turned on national search without police knowledge, and recommended 30-day deletion and SFPD control of Nationwide Lookup.

hops.notes: Verified 19:50 by Research: AG bulletin quotes (pp.2-3) checked against the PDF text; the bulletin says nothing about a court-order exception, so SFPD's 'court order or warrant' wording is SFPD's own. The 1.6M figure is the SF Standard's own count of SFPD search logs (not statewide); the lawsuit repeats it as an allegation. SFPD policy PDF returned 403 tonight, so the SFPD quote is from the afternoon fetch. HRC (Mission Local, Sept 28 2026) and SFPD biannual report (Nationwide Lookup Aug 2024-Feb 2025, enabled without Department knowledge) confirmed.
hops.plain: State law bars sharing with out-of-state police. For about 6 months, Flock left SF's data open to them anyway.

to.name: Federal agencies (DEA, IRS, US Marshals, CBP/HSI elsewhere)

hops.what_moves: Plate searches run on behalf of federal agencies

rules.summary: Federal agencies are not 'public agencies' under SB 34, so sharing with them is not allowed.
rules.quote: the definition of 'public agency' is limited to state or local agencies, including law enforcement agencies, and does not include out-of-state or federal law enforcement agencies.

rules.summary: NCRIC says it will not share with federal law enforcement or for immigration enforcement.
rules.quote: The NCRIC will not share, disseminate, or sell any law enforcement data to law enforcement agencies outside California, federal law enforcement, any private entities or individuals

rules.summary: Even where the Values Act (SB 54) might allow a disclosure, SB 34 still restricts ALPR sharing.
rules.quote: Even where the sharing of license plate data may be for a permitted purpose under SB 54, all agencies should be aware that there are strict privacy limitations on the sharing of license plate reader data

rules.summary: SFPD says its ALPR data is not used for immigration enforcement, citing SF's sanctuary ordinance.
rules.quote: ALPR data collected by SFPD is not used for the enforcement of Immigration Laws. SFPD complies with SF Admin Code Section 12H and 12I.

retention.summary: Not applicable: federal agencies should not receive the data at all.

breaches.summary: Of the 299 WSIN queries of SF's network, Mission Local names the DEA, IRS, US Marshals and US Forest Service among the requesters. SFPD says none were ICE/DHS or referenced immigration.
Flock paused its pilots with CBP and HSI after an Illinois audit found CBP had accessed Illinois data.
Logs showed local police nationwide running Flock lookups for or about ICE, a 'side door' since ICE has no Flock contract. Not SF-specific.

hops.notes: Flock now says federal agencies are excluded from statewide and national lookup and that immigration- and reproductive-care-related searches are auto-blocked in CA.
hops.plain: Federal agencies are also off-limits under state law. An SFPD audit found 299 searches run on their behalf.
